# ROSE: An Intent-Centered Evaluation Metric for NL2SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#rose)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.257.pdf) · ACL 2026 proceedings version, pages 5682–5709

**Reading coverage:** All 28 pages: main sections 1–7, limitations, references and Appendices A–O including every acceptance rule and example prompt; Figures 1–6 visually inspected.

## Research question

Reference-query execution matching can reject plausible interpretations or propagate flawed gold SQL, while an unconstrained LLM judge can accept too much.

## Method

ROSE checks executability, invokes a reference-independent Prover only for execution mismatches, and challenges accepted predictions with a Refuter that sees the reference SQL. Explicit acceptance conventions govern ambiguity, duplicates, ties and formatting.

## Evaluation

ROSE-VEC contains 585 predictions retained after exact agreement between two of five experienced graduate annotators. Human raters could see gold SQL and execution matches. The paper compares several reasoning backbones, ablates reference access and the cascade, audits errors and re-scores 19 methods on BIRD Mini-Dev.

## What the results support

The o3 implementation reaches 80.43% kappa versus FLEX’s 56.70%, an improvement of 23.73 percentage points. Refutation improves overall agreement; diagnostic precision varies sharply by backbone and dataset, especially for ambiguous BIRD questions.

## Limits and qualifications

Consensus filtering excludes disputed cases, and the judge embodies chosen conventions rather than recovering an individual user’s intent. The appendix prompts stipulate an inclusive interpretation of “after” a specified year. Model-version differences confound the observational claim that base models dominate engineering; this is not a controlled causal comparison.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful as a semantic evaluator and source of diagnostic leads, with versioned judges and explicit acceptance rules. Its ambiguity labels and leaderboard changes need independent checks before treating them as ground truth.
